title: The system: a game backend with Redis in four roles
caption: Redis keeps the fast, rebuildable state (sessions, counters, boards, live events); the player DB stays the source of truth.

steps.text: Every call reaches the gateway, which first increments a per-player counter that expires with its window: one round trip of well under 1 ms.
The gateway resolves the session token with one hash read. Each request refreshes the TTL, so idle sessions disappear on their own.
A match ends: the game API writes the result to the player DB first, then adds the points to this week's sorted set.
Reading the board is a range of the sorted set for the top 100 plus one rank lookup for the player: both O(log n).
A friend comes online: the social API publishes on that player's channel, and whichever push gateway holds the socket forwards it.
Redis holds derived data only. If a board is lost, the rebuilder replays match results from the DB and refills the sorted set.

scenarios.name: Tournament final
scenarios.summary: Score writes jump tenfold for an hour. Throughput per node is fine; the risk is one board key living on one node.

steps.text: A live tournament ends; hundreds of thousands of matches finish within minutes.
Every result updates the same tournament board key, so one Redis node takes all of it.
The game API batches: it sums points per player for 200 ms and sends them pipelined, turning thousands of commands into a few round trips.
Rate counters protect the gateway from clients that retry too eagerly.

scenarios.name: Session primary fails
scenarios.summary: The session store's primary dies: a replica takes over in seconds, and the last moment of writes may be gone.

steps.text: The session primary stops answering; logins and token checks start timing out.
Rate checks fail open for a few seconds rather than block every player.
Sentinel promotes a replica (about 10–30 s). Sessions created in the last second before the crash were never replicated, so those players log in again.

scenarios.name: Push gateway deploy
scenarios.summary: Pub/sub is fire and forget: a gateway that is restarting misses every message sent meanwhile.

steps.text: A rolling deploy restarts push gateways one at a time; their sockets reconnect to other gateways.
Messages published during the gap reach no subscriber and are dropped, with no error to the publisher.
On reconnect, the client asks the social API for anything since its last seen message id, read from the DB. Must-deliver data never relies on pub/sub alone.
